objects.description: Error correction level for QR Codes, in ascending order of protection: LOW, MEDIUM, QUARTILE, HIGH.
Mask pattern selector for QR Codes. Use AUTO for automatic selection or 0–7 to force a specific mask.
Data mode identifiers for segments: numeric, alphanumeric, byte, kanji, and ECI designator.

Represents one data/control segment to be encoded into a QR Code. Contains mode, character count, pointer to bit-packed data buffer, and its bit length. Users can create segments via factory functions or by manually filling fields, respecting length and mode invariants.

functions.name: qrcodegen_encodeText
functions.signature: bool qrcodegen_encodeText(const char *text, uint8_t tempBuffer[], uint8_t qrcode[], enum qrcodegen_Ecc ecl, int minVersion, int maxVersion, enum qrcodegen_Mask mask, bool boostEcl);
functions.description: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into a QR Code symbol. Chooses the smallest version within the given range that fits the data; may elevate ECC level if boostEcl is true and it does not increase the version. On success, writes an encoded QR Code into qrcode, which can be inspected with qrcodegen_getSize() and qrcodegen_getModule(). Returns false if the data cannot fit at the requested ECC and version range.
requirements: text must be UTF-8 encoded and contain no NUL characters (embedded '\0').
Require 1 <= minVersion <= maxVersion <= 40.
mask must be qrcodegen_Mask_AUTO or one of qrcodegen_Mask_0..qrcodegen_Mask_7.
Let len = qrcodegen_BUFFER_LEN_FOR_VERSION(maxVersion); both tempBuffer[0:len] and qrcode[0:len] must be readable/writable and at least len bytes long.
tempBuffer and qrcode arrays must not overlap (no aliasing).
Initial contents of tempBuffer and qrcode may be uninitialized (function writes before reads).
On return, tempBuffer contents are not useful and should be treated as uninitialized.
Callers must check the bool return value for success before using qrcode.

functions.name: qrcodegen_encodeBinary
functions.signature: bool qrcodegen_encodeBinary(uint8_t dataAndTemp[], size_t dataLen, uint8_t qrcode[], enum qrcodegen_Ecc ecl, int minVersion, int maxVersion, enum qrcodegen_Mask mask, bool boostEcl);
functions.description: Encodes a sequence of bytes into a QR Code symbol using byte mode. Chooses the smallest version within the given range that fits the data; may elevate ECC level if boostEcl is true and it does not increase the version. On success, writes the QR Code to qrcode, which can be read with qrcodegen_getSize() and qrcodegen_getModule(). Returns false if the data cannot fit at the requested ECC and version range.
requirements: Require 1 <= minVersion <= maxVersion <= 40.
mask must be qrcodegen_Mask_AUTO or one of qrcodegen_Mask_0..qrcodegen_Mask_7.
Let len = qrcodegen_BUFFER_LEN_FOR_VERSION(maxVersion); both dataAndTemp[0:len] and qrcode[0:len] must be readable/writable and at least len bytes long.
dataAndTemp and qrcode arrays must not overlap (no aliasing).
The range dataAndTemp[0:dataLen] contains the input bytes (any values allowed; valid UTF-8 is suggested but not required).
The ranges dataAndTemp[dataLen:len] and qrcode[0:len] may be uninitialized before the call (function writes before reads).
After return, dataAndTemp contains no useful data and should be treated as uninitialized.
Callers must check the bool return value for success before using qrcode.

functions.name: qrcodegen_encodeSegments
functions.signature: bool qrcodegen_encodeSegments(const struct qrcodegen_Segment segs[], size_t len, enum qrcodegen_Ecc ecl, uint8_t tempBuffer[], uint8_t qrcode[]);
functions.description: Encodes a custom list of segments into a QR Code at or above the requested ECC level, automatically choosing the smallest fitting version. May internally boost ECC if it does not increase the version. This low-level API lets you mix modes for better compression. On success, writes the QR Code to qrcode, readable via qrcodegen_getSize() and qrcodegen_getModule().
requirements: Let bufLen = qrcodegen_BUFFER_LEN_FOR_VERSION(qrcodegen_VERSION_MAX); tempBuffer[0:bufLen] and qrcode[0:bufLen] must be readable/writable and at least bufLen bytes long.
tempBuffer and qrcode arrays must not overlap (no aliasing).
Initial contents of tempBuffer and qrcode may be uninitialized (function writes before reads).
The input array segs may contain segments whose data buffers overlap with tempBuffer.
After return, tempBuffer is not useful and should be treated as uninitialized.
After return, any segment whose data buffer overlaps tempBuffer[0:bufLen] must be treated as having invalid values in that array.
Callers must check the bool return value before using qrcode.
segs must describe valid segments: each segment’s numChars and bitLength must conform to its mode and data buffer (per struct contract).

functions.name: qrcodegen_isNumeric
functions.description: Checks whether a string can be encoded in numeric mode (i.e., all characters are digits '0'..'9'). Returns true iff the entire string is numeric.
requirements: text should be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Only characters '0'..'9' are permitted; any other character makes the function return false.

functions.name: qrcodegen_isAlphanumeric
functions.description: Checks whether a string can be encoded in alphanumeric mode. Allowed set: digits 0–9, uppercase A–Z, space, $, %, *, +, -, ., /, :. Returns true iff all characters are in this set.
requirements: text should be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Only the following characters are permitted: '0'..'9', 'A'..'Z', space, '$', '%', '*', '+', '-', '.', '/', ':'; any other character makes the function return false.

functions.name: qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize
functions.signature: size_t qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize(enum qrcodegen_Mode mode, size_t numChars);
functions.description: Computes the number of bytes required for the data buffer of a segment with the specified mode and number of characters. Returns SIZE_MAX on failure (e.g., too many characters or required bits exceed INT16_MAX). For ECI mode, numChars must be 0 and the returned size is a worst-case bound; for other modes the result is exact.
requirements: If the calculation would exceed INT16_MAX bits or if numChars > INT16_MAX, the function returns SIZE_MAX and callers must treat this as failure.
For byte mode, numChars is the number of bytes (not Unicode code points).
For ECI mode, numChars must be 0; the returned size is a worst-case upper bound.
Valid results are in [0, ceil(INT16_MAX/8)] (at most 4096); callers should allocate at least the returned number of bytes for the segment data buffer.
Callers must handle SIZE_MAX return as an error condition and avoid using it as a buffer size.

functions.name: qrcodegen_makeBytes
functions.signature: struct qrcodegen_Segment qrcodegen_makeBytes(const uint8_t data[], size_t len, uint8_t buf[]);
functions.description: Creates a segment representing the given binary data encoded in byte mode. Any byte sequence is acceptable. Use qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize(qrcodegen_Mode_BYTE, len) to size buf before calling. Returns a qrcodegen_Segment describing the segment backed by buf.
requirements: buf must have capacity at least qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize(qrcodegen_Mode_BYTE, len) bytes.
data points to len bytes of input; any values 0x00..0xFF are allowed.
The returned segment’s fields (mode, numChars, data, bitLength) assume buf remains valid and unmodified for as long as the segment is used.

functions.name: qrcodegen_makeNumeric
functions.signature: struct qrcodegen_Segment qrcodegen_makeNumeric(const char *digits, uint8_t buf[]);
functions.description: Creates a numeric-mode segment from a null-terminated string of decimal digits. Returns a qrcodegen_Segment describing the segment backed by buf.
requirements: digits must be a null-terminated string containing only characters '0'..'9' (use qrcodegen_isNumeric to validate).
Let n = strlen(digits); buf must have capacity at least qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize(qrcodegen_Mode_NUMERIC, n) bytes.
The returned segment assumes buf remains valid and unmodified for as long as the segment is used.

functions.name: qrcodegen_makeAlphanumeric
functions.signature: struct qrcodegen_Segment qrcodegen_makeAlphanumeric(const char *text, uint8_t buf[]);
functions.description: Creates an alphanumeric-mode segment from a null-terminated string using the QR alphanumeric character set (0–9, A–Z, space, $, %, *, +, -, ., /, :). Returns a qrcodegen_Segment describing the segment backed by buf.
requirements: text must be a null-terminated string containing only the allowed alphanumeric set (use qrcodegen_isAlphanumeric to validate).
Let n = strlen(text); buf must have capacity at least qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize(qrcodegen_Mode_ALPHANUMERIC, n) bytes.
The returned segment assumes buf remains valid and unmodified for as long as the segment is used.

functions.name: qrcodegen_makeEci
functions.signature: struct qrcodegen_Segment qrcodegen_makeEci(long assignVal, uint8_t buf[]);
functions.description: Creates a segment representing an Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI) designator with the given assignment value. The segment is backed by buf and can be combined with other segments to signal an alternate character set or interpretation.
requirements: For ECI mode, qrcodegen_calcSegmentBufferSize must be called with mode=qrcodegen_Mode_ECI and numChars=0 to size buf (uses worst-case size).
assignVal is the ECI assignment value; valid ranges are defined by the QR Code specification (exact constraints unknown in this header).
The returned segment assumes buf remains valid and unmodified for as long as the segment is used.

functions.name: qrcodegen_getSize
functions.description: Returns the side length (modules per side) of a previously generated QR Code contained in qrcode. The result is in [21, 177].
requirements: qrcode must point to a buffer previously filled by a successful qrcodegen_encode* function call.
Callers should not assume any particular buffer length beyond that required when it was created (qrcodegen_BUFFER_LEN_FOR_VERSION(version)).

functions.name: qrcodegen_getModule
functions.signature: bool qrcodegen_getModule(const uint8_t qrcode[], int x, int y);
functions.description: Returns the color of the module at coordinates (x,y) in the given QR Code: true for dark, false for light. Returns false if the coordinates are out of bounds.
requirements: qrcode must point to a buffer previously filled by a successful qrcodegen_encode* function call.
Top-left coordinate is (x=0, y=0).
If x or y is out of bounds, the function returns false (light).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for UTF-8 text without NUL, tailored for qrcodegen_encodeText usage.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid UTF-8, no embedded NULs
# - Vary content to exercise different QR encoding modes and sizes
# - Keep length within typical QR capacity for versions 1..10 used in some stubs
# - Randomized but reproducible via seed
# - Return as bytes (no NUL byte in payload)

# Character pools for different QR modes
_DIGITS = "0123456789"
_ALNUM = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ $%*+-./:"
# Some common multi-byte UTF-8 characters to trigger BYTE mode and varied code point lengths
# Include 2-, 3-, and 4-byte sequences
_MULTI_UTF8 = [
    # 2-byte (Latin-1 supplement examples)
    "é", "ñ", "ø", "ß", "£", "¢", "§",
    # 3-byte (Greek, Cyrillic, CJK)
    "Ω", "Ж", "☺", "中", "文", "日", "本",
    # 4-byte (emoji)
    "😀", "🚀", "🌟", "🧪", "🧩", "📦",
]

# Some structured patterns known to be valid and interesting for QR encoders
_STRUCTURED_EXAMPLES = [
    "HELLO WORLD",
    "HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM",
    "HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/ABC-123",
    "WIFI:S:MyNetwork;T:WPA;P:password123;;",
    "mailto:user@example.com",
    "SMSTO:+1234567890:HELLO",
    "BEGIN:VCARD\nVERSION:3.0\nN:Doe;John;;;\nFN:John Doe\nEND:VCARD",
]

def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(_ALNUM) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_digits(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(_DIGITS) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_bytes_text(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Produce arbitrary bytes-like text using full Unicode but avoiding NUL
    # We build from ASCII plus chosen multibyte chars to ensure valid UTF-8
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.70:
            # Common ASCII, avoid NUL; include spaces and punctuation
            c = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_.,:/+%$*#@!()[]{}?&=\"'\\")
            parts.append(c)
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(_MULTI_UTF8))
    return "".join(parts)

def _pick_length_for_versions(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # The fuzz stubs use versions up to 10 in some cases; conservative lengths
    # Version 1-L capacity ~41 alnum or 17 bytes; Version 10 can handle far more.
    # Choose a bimodal distribution: small (0-25) and medium (26-200)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.randint(0, 25)
    else:
        return rng.randint(26, 200)

def _compose_segments_style(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create texts that encourage specific modes or mixtures:
    style = rng.choices(
        population=["numeric", "alnum", "url", "wifi", "vcard", "email", "sms", "mixed", "unicode"],
        weights=[15, 20, 10, 5, 5, 10, 5, 20, 10],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if style == "numeric":
        return _rand_digits(rng, _pick_length_for_versions(rng))
    if style == "alnum":
        return _rand_alnum(rng, _pick_length_for_versions(rng)).upper()
    if style == "url":
        host = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 10)).upper()
        path = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(0, 20)).replace(" ", "")
        scheme = rng.choice(["http", "https"]) + "://"
        tld = rng.choice([".com", ".org", ".net", ".io", ".dev"]).lower()
        extra = ""
        if rng.random() < 0.5 and path:
            extra = "/" + path
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            extra += "?q=" + _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(1, 10))
        return scheme + host.lower() + tld + extra
    if style == "wifi":
        ssid = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(4, 12)).replace(":", "_")
        pwd = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(8, 16)).replace(";", "_")
        t = rng.choice(["WPA", "WEP"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else "nopass"
        return f"WIFI:S:{ssid};T:{t};P:{pwd};;"
    if style == "vcard":
        first = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 8)).title()
        last = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 10)).title()
        return f"BEGIN:VCARD\nVERSION:3.0\nN:{last};{first};;;\nFN:{first} {last}\nEND:VCARD"
    if style == "email":
        user = (_rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 10))).replace(" ", "").lower()
        dom = (_rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 8))).replace(" ", "").lower()
        tld = rng.choice(["com", "org", "net", "io", "dev"])
        return f"mailto:{user}@{dom}.{tld}"
    if style == "sms":
        num = "+" + _rand_digits(rng, rng.randint(9, 12))
        msg = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 20))
        return f"SMSTO:{num}:{msg}"
    if style == "mixed":
        # Mix numeric, alnum, and some unicode to push BYTE mode
        parts = [
            _rand_digits(rng, rng.randint(1, 10)),
            "-",
            _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 12)),
            " ",
            rng.choice(_MULTI_UTF8),
            _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(0, 6)),
        ]
        return "".join(parts)
    # unicode
    base = _rand_bytes_text(rng, rng.randint(5, 60))
    return base

def _maybe_pick_structured(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        s = rng.choice(_STRUCTURED_EXAMPLES)
        # Optionally append small random tail staying alnum to remain valid
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s += " " + _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(1, 10))
        return s
    return ""

def _ensure_valid_utf8_no_nul(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode to UTF-8; replace is safe but we try to only construct valid characters.
    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    # Ensure no NULs; our generation avoids NUL, but double-check and strip if any
    if 0 in b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")
    return b

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide composition strategy
    use_structured = rng.random() < 0.35
    if use_structured:
        base = _maybe_pick_structured(rng)
        if not base:
            base = _compose_segments_style(rng)
    else:
        base = _compose_segments_style(rng)

    # Occasionally concatenate multiple parts to increase length and mode variety
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        extra_parts = [
            _compose_segments_style(rng),
            (" " if rng.random() < 0.7 else "\n"),
            _compose_segments_style(rng),
        ]
        base = base + "".join(extra_parts)

    # Trim to stay under 4096 bytes and typical QR capacities used by stubs
    b = _ensure_valid_utf8_no_nul(base)
    # Hard cap to 1000 bytes to remain safe for version <= 10 in stubs; still valid input if it doesn't fit
    if len(b) > 1000:
        b = b[:1000]
        # Ensure not cutting inside a multibyte sequence by decoding best-effort then re-encode
        # Decode ignoring errors and re-encode, guaranteeing valid UTF-8
        try:
            b = b.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore').encode('utf-8')
        except Exception:
            # Fallback: keep slice (it will likely still be valid due to generation method)
            pass

    # Guarantee non-empty sometimes, empty sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        return b""  # empty string is allowed

    # Ensure the string has no embedded NULs (already enforced)
    if 0 in b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")

    return b[:4096]

import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets QR code encoding APIs that accept arbitrary binary data and
# also use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to fill bytes. We therefore return a bytes buffer that,
# when used as the source string or input data region, yields interesting but valid
# byte sequences of varying lengths, covering edge cases and diverse content.

_MAX_OUT = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_pattern(pattern: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(total, len(pattern))
    return pattern * reps + pattern[:rem]

def _utf8_examples() -> list[bytes]:
    # Valid UTF-8 sequences (even though not required, may exercise UTF-8 paths)
    return [
        "".encode(),
        "Hello, World!".encode(),
        "0123456789".encode(),
        "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".encode(),
        "$.+ -*/:/%".encode(),
        "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
        "𝄞🎵🎶".encode("utf-8"),
        "äöüÄÖÜß".encode("utf-8"),
    ]

def _alnum_table() -> bytes:
    # QR alphanumeric set: 0-9, A-Z, space, $, %, *, +, -, ., /, :
    return b"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ $%*+-./:"

def _edge_patterns() -> list[bytes]:
    # Patterns that are useful for QR encoding paths
    patt = []
    patt.append(b"")
    patt.append(b"0" * 1)
    patt.append(b"0" * 2)
    patt.append(b"0" * 3)
    patt.append(b"0" * 10)
    patt.append(b"9" * 127)
    patt.append(b"A" * 128)
    patt.append(b"Z" * 255)
    patt.append(b" " * 256)
    patt.append(b"$%*+-./:" * 64)
    patt.append(_alnum_table())
    patt.append(bytes(range(256)))                 # 0..255 once
    patt.append(bytes(reversed(range(256))))       # 255..0 once
    patt.append(b"\x00" * 512)                    # lots of zeros
    patt.append(b"\xFF" * 512)
    patt.append(b"\xAA\x55" * 256)               # alternating pattern
    patt.append(b"\x00\xFF" * 256)
    patt.append(b"\x11\x22\x33\x44" * 128)
    return patt

def _construct_interesting_source(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose a source string that fuzzer consumes cyclically. Ensure length >= 1.
    # Mix of UTF-8 text, numeric/alnum, and arbitrary binary to hit diverse code paths.
    choices: list[bytes] = []

    # UTF-8 examples
    choices.extend(_utf8_examples())

    # Alphanumeric sequences of varying lengths
    table = _alnum_table()
    for n in (1, 2, 3, 10, 47, 97, 251):
        seq = _repeat_pattern(table, n)
        choices.append(seq)

    # Numeric sequences
    for n in (1, 2, 3, 11, 100, 512):
        digits = _repeat_pattern(b"0123456789", n)
        choices.append(digits)

    # Edge binary patterns
    choices.extend(_edge_patterns())

    # Random blobs of various sizes
    for n in (7, 13, 29, 64, 128, 257, 511, 1023):
        choices.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))

    # Combine 2-4 randomly chosen chunks and possibly truncate/extend with random tail
    k = rng.randint(2, 4)
    parts = [rng.choice(choices) for _ in range(k)]
    base = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not base:
        base = b"X"

    # Optionally adjust length to better match target_len locality for data copy loops
    if target_len == 0:
        return base

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Expand with a repeated signature so modulo indexing yields structure
        sigs = [b"QR", b"\x00\xFF", b"ALNUM:", b"NUM:", b"BYTE:"]
        sig = rng.choice(sigs)
        need = rng.randint(0, max(0, target_len * 2))
        base += _repeat_pattern(sig, need)

    # Cap the source to a reasonable size so total output remains bounded
    if len(base) > _MAX_OUT:
        base = base[:_MAX_OUT]

    # Guarantee at least 1 byte for FUZZ_PARAM_STR contract
    if len(base) == 0:
        base = b"X"

    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # The fuzzers use two main styles:
    # - encodeBinary: picks dataLen in [0,len] and fills dataAndTemp[i] = src[i % src.size()].
    #   Our bytes become src. Therefore, we want src non-empty, and structured so modulo repeats
    #   produce meaningful content across many lengths.
    # - makeBytes/make* segments: also use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for raw byte sources.
    # We return a single buffer designed to be consumed as that source string.

    # Choose a plausible target length heuristic to shape the source composition
    # toward QR capacity edges but remain <= 4096.
    target_len = rng.choice([
        0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 10, 25, 47, 64, 120, 240, 500, 1024, 2048, 3072
    ])

    src = _construct_interesting_source(rng, target_len)

    # Final safety bound
    if len(src) > _MAX_OUT:
        src = src[:_MAX_OUT]

    # Ensure at least one byte
    if not src:
        src = b"X"

    return src

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, choices: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    return rng.choice(choices)

# Build interesting strings covering numeric, alphanumeric, mixed, edge cases, UTF-8, and lengths.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects a C string without embedded NUL; we must avoid '\x00' inside.
# We'll generate UTF-8 or binary-like but non-NUL bytes, and ensure it's null-terminated by fuzzer infra.

_ALNUM_SET = b"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ $%*+\-\./:"
_DIGITS = b"0123456789"

# Some reusable interesting samples (no NULs)
_BASE_SAMPLES = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"0",
    b"9",
    b"0000000000",
    b"1234567890",
    b"42",
    b"A",
    b"HELLO WORLD",
    b"QR-CODE:2026/01+",
    b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ",
    b"$%*+-. /:",
    b"a",  # will fail alphanumeric predicate
    b"hello",
    b"123ABC",
    b"ABC123XYZ",
    b"99999999999999999999",
    b"   ",
    b"--..//::",
]

# Some valid multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (no NULs)
_UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "π≈3.14159".encode("utf-8"),
    "漢字かなカナ".encode("utf-8"),
    "emoji😀😃😄".encode("utf-8"),
    "€uro".encode("utf-8"),
    "Привет".encode("utf-8"),
]

# Binary-like bytes avoiding NUL (0x00)
def _random_bytes_no_nul(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.randrange(1, 256) for _ in range(length))

# Numeric-only generator
def _gen_numeric(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.choice(_DIGITS) for _ in range(length))

# Alphanumeric-set generator (allowed by qrcodegen_isAlphanumeric)
def _gen_alnum_set(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.choice(_ALNUM_SET) for _ in range(length))

# Mixed invalid for alnum (introduce lowercase or other symbols)
def _gen_mixed_invalid(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    pool = _ALNUM_SET + b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz@#^&()[]{}_=~`|\\\"'?,;!"  # still avoid NUL
    return bytes(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(length))

# Create strings with leading/trailing spaces and punctuation
def _gen_spaced(rng: random.Random, core: bytes) -> bytes:
    left = b" " * rng.randint(0, 5)
    right = b" " * rng.randint(0, 5)
    sep = _rand_choice(rng, [b"", b"-", b"/", b":", b".", b"+"])
    return left + core + sep + right

# Ensure no embedded NULs (fuzzer expects C string). Our generators already avoid NUL; keep guard.
def _sanitize_no_nul(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    if b"\x00" in b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
    return b

def _assemble_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    samples = list(_BASE_SAMPLES)
    samples += _UTF8_SAMPLES

    # Numeric edge lengths: 1, 2, 3, 10, 50, 256, 1000 (bounded by 4096 limit later)
    for n in [1, 2, 3, 10, 50, 256, 1000]:
        samples.append(_gen_numeric(rng, n))

    # Alphanumeric valid strings at various lengths
    for n in [1, 5, 13, 47, 200]:
        samples.append(_gen_alnum_set(rng, n))

    # Mixed invalid for alnum but sometimes numeric prefix/suffix
    for n in [5, 20, 100]:
        m = _gen_mixed_invalid(rng, n)
        # Add numeric prefix/suffix sometimes
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            m = _gen_numeric(rng, rng.randint(1, 8)) + m
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            m = m + _gen_numeric(rng, rng.randint(1, 8))
        samples.append(m)

    # Structured patterns
    samples.append(b"000123456789")                 # leading zeros
    samples.append(b"12345678901234567890")         # long numeric
    samples.append(b"CODE-128/QR:ABC123")           # valid alnum
    samples.append(b"lowercase-is-invalid-for-alnum")
    samples.append(b"MIXED Case 123")

    # Random binary-like but non-NUL bytes
    for n in [8, 32, 128, 512]:
        samples.append(_random_bytes_no_nul(rng, n))

    # Spaced variants
    samples += [_gen_spaced(rng, core) for core in [b"12345", b"HELLO", b"DATA", b"A1B2C3"]]

    # Combine UTF-8 with ASCII
    for u in _UTF8_SAMPLES:
        samples.append(u + b" QR")
        samples.append(b"ID:" + _gen_numeric(rng, 6) + b" " + u)

    # Ensure sizes not exceeding 4096 when used directly
    return [s if len(s) <= 4096 else s[:4096] for s in samples]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of candidates
    candidates = _assemble_candidates(rng)

    # Also build on-the-fly constructed cases with version/ECC-like tokens to vary semantics
    tokens = [
        b"ECC:L", b"ECC:M", b"ECC:Q", b"ECC:H",
        b"MASK:0", b"MASK:7", b"AUTO",
        b"VER:1", b"VER:40",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        t = rng.sample(tokens, rng.randint(1, min(4, len(tokens))))
        core = _gen_alnum_set(rng, rng.randint(3, 40))
        combo = b" ".join(t + [core])
        candidates.append(combo)

    # Choose a candidate with weighted preferences to exercise both predicates
    weights = []
    for s in candidates:
        if all(c in _DIGITS for c in s):
            weights.append(3.0)  # numeric emphasis
        elif all(c in _ALNUM_SET for c in s):
            weights.append(2.0)  # alnum valid
        else:
            weights.append(1.0)  # invalid for alnum, still valid C string

    choice = rng.choices(candidates, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

    # Slight chance to adjust length by repeating or slicing, staying <=4096 and non-empty allowed
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(choice) > 0:
        reps = rng.randint(2, max(2, 4096 // max(1, len(choice))))
        choice = (choice * reps)[:4096]
    elif rng.random() < 0.3 and len(choice) > 10:
        # slice a middle segment
        start = rng.randint(0, len(choice) - 10)
        end = start + rng.randint(10, min(200, len(choice) - start))
        choice = choice[start:end]

    # Ensure no NUL bytes
    choice = _sanitize_no_nul(choice)

    # Bound size
    if len(choice) > 4096:
        choice = choice[:4096]

    return choice

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for inputs to fuzz qrcodegen segment-based encoders.
# Target stubs construct segments of types: BYTE, NUMERIC, ALPHANUMERIC, ECI.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR supplies arbitrary byte sequences that get copied into BYTE segments.
# Providing a buffer that contains a mix of useful patterns will exercise:
# - Short/long lengths (stub chooses 0..511 for length; data is cycled modulo our buffer size)
# - Numeric-only runs (to compare compression modes when other segments are numeric)
# - Alphanumeric runs (valid for ALPHANUMERIC mode)
# - UTF-8 multibyte sequences (to stress BYTE handling vs text assumptions elsewhere)
# - Binary bytes including NUL, 0xFF, and repeating patterns
# The stub takes the string length >= 1, and indexes data[k % data.size()].
# Hence our buffer should be reasonably sized, <=4096.

ALNUM_TABLE = b"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ $%*+-./:"

def _rand_numeric(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(ord('0') + r.randrange(10) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_alnum(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(ALNUM_TABLE[r.randrange(len(ALNUM_TABLE))] for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_samples() -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        # ASCII words
        b"HELLO WORLD 12345",
        # Mixed Latin-1 sequences (as bytes; not necessarily valid UTF-8)
        bytes([0xC3, 0x89, 0xC3, 0xA9, 0x20, 0xC2, 0xA3]),  # \'\u00C9\u00E9 \u00A3 in UTF-8
        # Valid multi-byte UTF-8 from various scripts
        "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
        "😀😃😄😁".encode("utf-8"),
        "汉字かなカナ".encode("utf-8"),
        # Common punctuation/symbols
        "$%*+-./: ".encode("ascii"),
    ]


def _binary_chunks(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Include NULs, 0xFF, incremental, repeating patterns
    chunks = [
        bytes([0x00] * r.randrange(8, 32)),
        bytes([0xFF] * r.randrange(8, 32)),
        bytes(range(0, r.randrange(16, 64))),
        bytes((i % 251) for i in range(r.randrange(32, 128))),
    ]
    return chunks


def _build_sections(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # Numeric heavy section to fit numeric mode perfectly
    sections.append(_rand_numeric(r, r.randrange(16, 128)))

    # Alphanumeric-only section
    sections.append(_rand_alnum(r, r.randrange(16, 128)))

    # Several UTF-8 samples
    utf = _utf8_samples()
    r.shuffle(utf)
    sections.extend(utf[: r.randrange(2, min(5, len(utf)) + 1)])

    # Binary chunks for BYTE mode
    sections.extend(_binary_chunks(r))

    # Short edge-case tokens
    edge_tokens = [b"0", b"9", b"A", b"Z", b" ", b":", b"$", b"+", b"-", b"/", b"."]
    r.shuffle(edge_tokens)
    sections.extend(edge_tokens[: r.randrange(3, len(edge_tokens))])

    # Include a long numeric run and long alnum run to allow cycling
    sections.append(_rand_numeric(r, r.randrange(256, 600)))
    sections.append(_rand_alnum(r, r.randrange(256, 600)))

    return sections


def _assemble(sections: List[bytes], max_len: int, r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Interleave sections in random order with separators chosen from acceptable sets
    r.shuffle(sections)
    out = bytearray()

    # Separators to encourage mode boundaries; include NUL and 0xFF to test raw BYTE
    seps = [b" ", b"::", b"--", b"$", b"/", b"+", b"*", bytes([0x00]), bytes([0xFF])]

    for sec in sections:
        if len(out) + len(sec) > max_len:
            # Truncate the section if it would exceed max_len
            take = max_len - len(out)
            if take <= 0:
                break
            out.extend(sec[:take])
            break
        out.extend(sec)
        # Maybe add a separator
        if len(out) < max_len and r.random() < 0.6:
            sep = seps[r.randrange(len(seps))]
            take = min(len(sep), max_len - len(out))
            out.extend(sep[:take])
            if len(out) >= max_len:
                break

    # Ensure non-empty and within bounds
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"0")
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a target size for the reusable data buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR will provide.
    # The stub will modulo-index into this buffer for BYTE segments up to 512 length.
    # Pick a size that is relatively prime to many values to diversify modulo patterns.
    candidate_sizes = [127, 191, 223, 257, 353, 509, 761, 997]
    max_len = candidate_sizes[r.randrange(len(candidate_sizes))]

    sections = _build_sections(r)

    data = _assemble(sections, min(4096, max_len), r)

    # Guarantee contains at least:
    # - A digit, an uppercase letter, an allowed punctuation, and a binary 0x00 byte
    required = [b"7", b"Q", b"/", bytes([0x00])]
    tail = bytearray()
    for req in required:
        if req not in data:
            tail.extend(req)
    if tail:
        # Append without exceeding size; if no space, overwrite last bytes
        if len(data) + len(tail) <= max_len:
            data = data + bytes(tail)
        else:
            base = bytearray(data)
            # Overwrite the end to keep size fixed
            replace = bytes(tail)[: max(0, min(len(tail), max_len))]
            base[-len(replace):] = replace
            data = bytes(base)

    # Ensure length >= 1 and <= 4096 as required
    if not data:
        data = b"0"
    return data
